 In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam
 Present
 The Honourable Mr.Justice P.G. Ajithkumar
 Wednesday, the 17th day of January 2024 / 27th Pousha, 1945

Sc 329/2017 Of The Additional Sessions Judge-I,(Special Court),Pathanamthitta

sentences.text:
MIDHUN AGED 35 YEARS S/O. PONNAMMA CHARIVUKALATHADATHIL  VEEDU,KOZHENCHERY EAST, KOZHENCHERY MURI &
 VILLAGE,PATHANAMTHITTA-689641 RESPONDENT/RESPONDENT:
 STATE OF KERALA REPRESENTED BY PUBLIC PROSECUTOR HIGH COURT OF  KERALA,ERNAKULAM , PIN - 682031  Application praying that in the circumstances stated therein the High Court be pleased to suspend the sentence imposed on the Applicant/Appellant,by judgment Conviction and sentence in S.C.No.329/2017 of the Court of the 1st Additional Sessions Judge,(Special Court),Pathanamthitta dated 29.11.2022,and release the applicant/appellant on bail,pending disposal of the above Criminal Appeal,so as to secure the ends of justice.

This Application coming on for orders upon perusing the application and upon hearing the arguments of M/S.M.T.SURESHKUMAR, MANJUSHA K,
SREELAKSHMI SABU, RESWIN A. KHADIR, Advocates for the petitioner,and of the PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the respondent,the court passed the following:
 p.t.o  P.G. AJITHKUMAR, J.
 -----------------------------------------------------
 Crl.A.No.123 of 2023  ------------------------------------------------------
 Dated this the 17th day of January, 2024  ORDER

The appellant has filed this petition under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973(Code).
The petitioner stands convicted and sentenced for offences punishable under Sections 363, 366 and 376 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860(IPC).

Following is the sentence imposed:
a) Rigorous imprisonment for a period of ten years and to pay fine of Rs.1,00,000/-
in default of payment to undergo rigorous imprisonment for twelve months u/s.376

1 IPC.
b) Rigorous imprisonment for a period of two years and to pay fine of Rs.20,000/- in default of payment to undergo rigorous imprisonment for one month u/s.363 IPC.
c ) Rigorous imprisonment for a period of five years and to pay fine of Rs.60,000/- in default of payment to undergo rigorous imprisonment for six months u/s.366 IPC.

2. The petitioner would contend that the conviction is based on insufficient and unreliable evidence,
and there is every chance to allow the appeal.
Therefore the petitioner is entitled to get the sentence suspended.
3. The learned Public Prosecutor has filed objections on behalf of the respondent.

4. It is contended that the petitioner after procuring custody of the victim, who was aged only 14 years, from her house, on the pretext of rescuing her from the assault by her father, brought her to the premises of a Government U.P. School and subjected her to rape.
The offence being serious and in the wake of possibility of the petitioner threatening and assaulting the victim as well as the witnesses, he cannot be released on bail.
It is the further contention that having sentenced for a period of 10 years, releasing the appellant on bail would send a wrong message to society.

The law laid down by the Apex Court in Preet Pal Singh v. State of Uttarpradesh and another[(2020) 8 SCC 645] is placed on reliance in order to fortify the contention that no sufficient reason is there to suspend the sentence imposed on the petitioner.

entities.text: Preet Pal Singh v. State of Uttarpradesh and another[(2020) 8 SCC 645]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
6. The longest term of sentence imposed is 10 years.

In a case where term sentence is imposed,
convict is entitled to get the sentence suspended unless there are sufficient reasons to deny him bail.
See Bhagwan Rama Shinde Gosai and others v. State of Gujarat [(1999) 4 SCC 421].

entities.text: Bhagwan Rama Shinde Gosai and others v. State of Gujarat [(1999) 4 SCC 421
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. The Apex Court held in Preet Pal Singh (supra), that unless there are strong and compelling reasons, sentence shall not be suspended.
The petitioner was on bail, during trial and has now been behind bars since the date of conviction.
The plea of the petitioner for suspension of sentence requires a serious consideration.
8. The incident occurred in the year 2010.
The petitioner was convicted on 29.11.2022.
He had undergone the ordeal of the trial for a period of 12 years.
There is no allegation that during the period of trial, there was any threat from the part of the petitioner to the victim or the witnesses.

Both of them hail from the same locality and when there was no allegation of any threat or attempt to influence the victim or the witnesses, it cannot be said that the petitioner will try to do any such thing, particularly, when he is already convicted.
All the same, he was sentenced to undergo imprisonment for a period 10 years and the offence committed was at a time when the victim was aged only 10 years.
But, it may not be possible to dispose of this appeal immediately.

Taking all such aspects into consideration, I am of the view that the sentence imposed on the petitioner can be Midhun vs State Of Kerala on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79329353/
2 suspended subject to strict conditions.
9.

Accordingly, this petition is allowed and the sentence imposed on the petitioner is suspended on his executing a bond for Rs.2,00,000/-(Rupees Two lakhs only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the trial court and subject to the following conditions:
i) The petitioner shall deposit the entire fine amount in the trial court within one month.
ii) The petitioner shall not involve in any offence during the pendency of the appeal.
iii) The petitioner shall not try to contact or cause any threat or intimidate the defacto complainant or any of the witnesses examined in the case.
In violation of any of the above conditions, the order suspending sentence is liable to be cancelled.

Sd/-
P.G. AJITHKUMAR, JUDGE PV 17-01-2024 /True Copy/ Assistant Registrar Midhun vs State Of Kerala on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79329353/
